questions.q: In Doverfield's SSO architecture, what role does Salesforce play relative to the corporate identity provider?
options: Salesforce is the Identity Provider, and the corporate IdP is the Service Provider
Salesforce is the Service Provider, trusting the corporate IdP's signed assertion instead of checking its own password
Salesforce and the corporate IdP both independently authenticate the user with no trust relationship
Salesforce replaces the need for an Identity Provider entirely
questions.explain: The IdP authenticates the user and vouches for their identity via a signed SAML assertion; Salesforce, as the Service Provider, trusts that assertion rather than validating a password of its own.

questions.q: What specifically does enabling Just-in-Time (JIT) provisioning do?
options: It deactivates a Salesforce user automatically when they are removed from the IdP
It automatically creates a Salesforce user account the first time that person successfully authenticates through the IdP via SAML, using attributes from the assertion
It immediately syncs every attribute change made in the IdP to Salesforce in real time, with no login required
It eliminates the need for a SAML SSO configuration
questions.explain: JIT provisioning creates the account on first successful SAML login using the assertion's attributes -- it does not continuously sync afterward, and it is triggered only by that first authentication.

questions.q: Why can't JIT provisioning be used to deactivate a user who has left the company?
options: A disabled or deactivated Salesforce user will not complete SAML authentication at all, so there is no login event for JIT to act on; deactivation has to happen through a separate offboarding step
JIT provisioning has a setting specifically to disable users that Doverfield simply hasn't turned on
SAML does not support sending any information about deactivated users
Deactivation can only be done through Named Credentials
questions.explain: JIT's mechanism is tied to a successful login -- a deactivated user can't log in at all, so JIT has no event to act on. The deactivation itself must come from a separate process.

questions.q: Why does Doverfield use the Federation ID field, rather than username, as its SAML identity-mapping key?
options: Federation ID is required by law for all SAML integrations
Username fields cannot be stored in Salesforce at all
Federation ID is a dedicated, stable key whose only job is identity mapping, decoupled from a username that may be email-shaped and can change over time
Federation ID is automatically generated from a user's password
questions.explain: Usernames can change when a person's email changes; a Federation ID is a dedicated field that stays stable regardless of what the person's login email happens to be, making it the more reliable mapping key.

questions.q: What does a signed SAML assertion from the IdP actually communicate to Salesforce?
options: The user's actual password, re-encrypted for Salesforce to decrypt
A statement that the user authenticated successfully, along with identifying attributes, which Salesforce validates and maps to a Salesforce user
A list of every system the user has ever logged into
A request for Salesforce to create a new IdP account
questions.explain: The assertion vouches for successful authentication and carries identifying attributes -- Salesforce's SAML SSO configuration defines how that assertion gets validated and mapped to a specific Salesforce user record.
